```plato

//==
// # Triply periodic minimal surfaces
//
// The implicit counterpart of a strut lattice: a smooth surface that repeats in
// all three axes and divides space into two interpenetrating labyrinths
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triply_periodic_minimal_surface). These are the
// standard nodal (short trigonometric) approximations, not the exact minimal
// surfaces — the exact ones have no closed form, and the nodal approximations
// are what every additive-manufacturing tool means by "gyroid".
//
// Two solids come from one surface, and they are different shapes: the NETWORK
// solid is one of the two labyrinths (the implicit at or below its level), and
// the SHEET solid is a wall of finite thickness straddling the surface itself.

// Which nodal approximation a triply periodic surface uses. Each is the
// classical short form: Gyroid is Schoen's gyroid, SchwarzPrimitive and
// SchwarzDiamond are Schwarz's P and D surfaces, Neovius is the Neovius
// surface, and IwpSurface is Schoen's I-WP.
type TpmsFamily = Gyroid | SchwarzPrimitive | SchwarzDiamond | Neovius | IwpSurface;
```
